papers.title: Recursive Synthesis for Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks

summary.tldr: Recursive Synthetic Terminal Tasks (RST) is a verified synthesis framework that recursively extends, realigns, and validates terminal tasks, producing 37,484 long-horizon agent tasks at approximately $0.05 per task.
key_points: Starting from seed tasks, RST extends reference solutions, realigns verifiers and instructions, and validates tasks in a fresh sandbox before using accepted outputs as seeds for subsequent rounds.
Over 15 rounds, median task solution lengths grew from 67 to 374 lines, median executed commands rose from 40 to 244, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro pass@4 fell from 90% to 2.5%.
Synthesis yield and validation rates remained stable through 15 rounds without reaching a scaling ceiling.
Fine-tuning Qwen3.5 models on rejection-sampled trajectories improved performance on terminal benchmarks by up to 10 points, while PPO lifted Qwen3.5-27B to 49.44% on Terminal-Bench 2.
summary.why_it_matters: RST provides a scalable, low-cost method to synthesize increasingly complex, verified training data for terminal agents, significantly boosting their performance on long-horizon benchmarks.

papers.title: AgentOPSD: Recursive Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: AgentOPSD is a critic-free agentic RL method that converts sparse outcome rewards into turn-level credit signals using recursive Bayesian belief updates on teacher-student log-probability gaps.
key_points: Aggregates token-level teacher-student log-probability gaps into turn-level evidence.
Recursively updates a Bayesian belief state in log-odds space to reweight turn-level credit without an auxiliary critic or extra rollouts.
Identifies pivotal decision turns by calculating the marginal belief revision between consecutive states.
Achieves an 89.1% success rate on ALFWorld using a Qwen2.5-7B model, outperforming GRPO and self-distillation baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides dense, turn-level credit assignment for complex multi-turn agent tasks without the computational overhead of training a separate critic network or generating extra rollout trajectories.

papers.title: WorldClaw: Agentic 3D Open-World Generation at Scale

summary.tldr: WorldClaw is a coarse-to-fine, agentic framework that generates large-scale, editable 3D open worlds from text prompts by combining LLM planning agents with terrain conditioning and render-based refinement agents.
key_points: Planning agents convert text prompts into structured specifications covering regions, terrain, assets, materials, and spatial relationships.
Global terrain foundations are built using semantic layouts, procedural/generative materials, reusable assets, and region-aware height fields.
Detail-demanding areas are populated with terrain-conditioned compositions and reconstructed as editable, textured instance-level meshes.
Render-based agents perform post-generation refinement on terrain, object placement, appearance, and physical contacts.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables the automated generation of massive, spatially coherent 3D environments with fully editable, instance-level assets suitable for downstream editing and interactive applications.

papers.title: EnvACE: Internalizing Environment Dynamics via World Rehearsal for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: EnvACE replaces external environment interactions during LLM agent RL training with end-to-end joint optimization of action generation and environment response rehearsal.
key_points: The policy alternates between generating tool calls and acting as the environment to produce and condition on rehearsed responses.
Both the acting and environment rehearsal roles are jointly optimized end-to-end using task-success rewards.
Internalizing environment dynamics in the model parameters allows private test-time rehearsal before committed action execution.
Evaluated on BFCL-v4, tau^2-Bench, VitaBench, and FinMCP-Bench, outperforming environment-scaling baselines across model scales.
summary.why_it_matters: EnvACE enables effective agentic RL scaling without the cost, verification bottlenecks, or grounding issues associated with building real or external environment simulators.

papers.title: Learning from Failures: Retrieval-Centric CoT via Hard Negatives for Unified Multimodal Retrieval

summary.tldr: UniME-R1 is an embedder-adviser framework that uses hard negatives to generate Retrieval-Centric Chain-of-Thought (RC-CoT) reasoning based on initial retrieval feedback rather than query-only context.
key_points: Identifies discriminative cues by having an adviser model analyze initial top-k retrieved candidates to determine where the embedder failed.
Reranks candidates directly if the target is in the top-k, or uses generated RC-CoT to perform full-corpus re-retrieval with a dual-mode embedder if it is missing.
Mines hard negatives to simulate retrieval failures during training.
Optimizes the adviser using supervised learning combined with retrieval-oriented reinforcement learning based on retrieval outcomes.
Demonstrates performance improvements across MMEB-V2 and general multimodal retrieval benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: Conditioning reasoning on actual retrieval failures allows Large Vision-Language Models to refine queries and resolve fine-grained ambiguities that direct encoding misses.

papers.title: ChronoVision: Temporal Reasoning via Latent State Reconstruction

summary.tldr: ChronoVision is a multimodal framework that enhances multi-step temporal reasoning by reconstructing latent image states and applying reinforcement learning with implicit process grounding and visual attention targeting.
key_points: Supervised fine-tuning uses a Reconstructive Visual Head to predict the latent final state and an ROI Attention Locating module driven by semantic span queries.
Reinforcement learning post-training employs a composite reward function assessing outcome correctness, latent process alignment, and unsupervised visual focus.
Introduces Vbvr-VQA, a benchmark dataset that evaluates video temporal tracking by reformulating reasoning into a strict image-ordering task.
Achieves 74.8% in-domain and 71.6% out-of-domain accuracy on Vbvr-VQA, and 55.0% accuracy on the IntPhys2 benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: It mitigates the ambiguity of language-only reasoning in MLLMs by grounding temporal visual transformations directly in the visual latent space.

papers.title: On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated On-Policy Distillation (OPD) and On-Policy Delta Distillation (OPD^2) for multilingual math reasoning using Qwen3 across English, Korean, and Japanese.
key_points: OPD^2 uses the probability gap between a post-trained teacher model and its base model as the training signal.
OPD^2 consistently outperformed standard OPD, yielding the largest improvements in Korean and Japanese while reducing the English-Korean performance gap.
English-only OPD improves Japanese and Korean performance but causes responses to shift toward English, demonstrating that multilingual data is necessary to maintain target-language outputs.
summary.why_it_matters: OPD^2 offers an effective alternative to reinforcement learning for multilingual post-training, but requires target-language data to prevent model outputs from drifting into English.

papers.title: GST-Bench: Can VLMs Develop Global Spatial Awareness from Video?

summary.tldr: GST-Bench evaluates global spatial intelligence in vision-language models using synthetic videos, exposing a massive performance gap between state-of-the-art models (42.68%) and humans (79.08%).
key_points: GST-Bench comprises human-verified VQA tasks derived from 6,790 minutes of synthetic video, requiring egocentric-to-global spatial mapping and unseen viewpoint inference.
Evaluation of 22 state-of-the-art VLMs showed a peak zero-shot accuracy of 42.68%, compared to the human benchmark of 79.08%.
A diagnostic subset, GST-Bench-Local, revealed that models succeed at local spatial tasks but fail to consolidate long-horizon visual streams into globally consistent scene representations.
The authors release GST-Train, a dedicated dataset designed to train models on global spatial reasoning tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: Current VLMs lack the global scene representation capabilities required for embodied agents to navigate and reason accurately across long-horizon continuous video.

papers.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization

summary.tldr: HarnessOpt-Bench is a new benchmark that evaluates LLMs on their ability to iteratively optimize agent harnesses (prompts, tools, and control flow) under stochastic, budget-constrained evaluation conditions.
key_points: HarnessOpt-Bench tests LLM optimizers using a target agent's seed harness, graded evaluation feedback, a fixed target-evaluation budget, and a held-out test set for final candidate scoring via normalized gain.
The benchmark uses a trusted execution environment to enforce evaluation boundaries, meter resource consumption, and archive candidate versions for auditability.
An evaluation of 5 frontier LLMs across 111 scored runs and 4 downstream tasks revealed that choice of optimizer model causes higher performance variance than the coding harness used.
Native harnesses did not consistently outperform a shared coding harness, with final optimization gains varying widely based on downstream tasks and seed regimes.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a standardized, discriminative protocol to measure and improve how effectively AI models can autonomously optimize the software environments of other agentic systems.

papers.title: K-EXAONE 2.0 Technical Report

summary.tldr: LG AI Research released K-EXAONE 2.0, an open-weight, Apache 2.0-licensed Mixture-of-Experts foundation model upcycled from K-EXAONE, featuring 750B total parameters, 37B active parameters, and a 256K token context window.
key_points: Architecture expands K-EXAONE into a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 750B total and ~37B activated parameters per token.
Supports context lengths up to 256K tokens and broadens multilingual coverage to ten languages.
Training pipeline utilizes continual pre-training, difficulty-focused mid-training, and post-training focused on reasoning, agentic coding, multilingualism, and Korean sociocultural safety.
Achieves primary performance gains in agentic coding, long-context understanding, long-context retrieval, and safety evaluations.
summary.why_it_matters: Its open-source Apache 2.0 license and low active-parameter ratio enable cost-effective deployment and research on high-capacity, long-context multilingual tasks.

papers.title: DyPES-VLA: Learning Shared Dynamics Priors and Embodiment-Specific Control for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation

summary.tldr: DyPES-VLA is a cross-embodiment Vision-Language-Action model that pairs shared dynamics priors trained via future-prediction objectives with an embodiment-specific Mixture-of-Experts action head operating directly in native action spaces.
key_points: Dynamics priors are learned by training a vision-language model with a future-prediction objective to capture object motion, contact, and scene changes from cross-embodiment data.
An embodiment-specific Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) action head converts shared priors into native action spaces without requiring manual action pre-alignment.
The MoE action head uses shared attention layers for temporal action structure alongside embodiment-specific feed-forward experts to handle kinematic constraints.
Achieves generalist performance of 98.0% success on LIBERO, 59.25% on RoboCasa-GR1, and 89.02% on RoboTwin 2.0.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the need for manual action space preprocessing, allowing a single generalist model to control diverse robot architectures using native control semantics.

papers.title: World-to-Wrist: Task-Conditioned Future Wrist Modeling for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation

summary.tldr: World-to-Wrist VLA introduces task-conditioned future wrist latent modeling and a structured annotation pipeline to improve fine-grained, contact-sensitive robot manipulation while maintaining over 80 Hz action-generation rates.
key_points: W2-VLA contextually couples vision-language models and a wrist predictor using latent modeling tokens derived from current multi-view inputs and instructions.
The wrist predictor uses the latent interface and wrist history to forecast future wrist latents, which are converted into context for action prediction.
The W2-CoT synthesis pipeline generates structured annotations covering task progress, physical transitions, and wrist-local evidence to supervise the latent interface.
Evaluated on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world hardware across single-arm and bimanual manipulation setups.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves the execution of precise, contact-heavy robotic tasks by explicitly predicting local wrist perspective changes within global task constraints without sacrificing real-time control speed.

papers.title: CalibForge: Adversarial Solver Calibration for Scaling Learnable Terminal Tasks

summary.tldr: CalibForge is an autonomous task synthesis system that uses multi-solver and contrastive adversarial calibration to revise executable terminal tasks into a solver-relative learnable zone for agent training.
key_points: CalibForge synthesizes tasks using two calibration strategies: multi-solver calibration to target solver disagreement, and contrastive calibration to target a strong-pass/weak-fail relation.
The system generated a dataset of 5,431 calibrated terminal tasks.
Models trained on the dataset achieved 32.58% and 47.57% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, outperforming baseline pipelines that rely solely on authoring, validation, or single-solver feedback.
Peak performance gains over base models reached 24.71 percentage points on Terminal-Bench 2.0, 27.68 points on SWE-bench Pro, and 30.04 points on Doc2Repo.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that calibrating synthesized tasks to solver ability creates more effective and transferable supervision data for training terminal execution agents.

papers.title: WorldCycle: Self-Verifiable Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Video World Models

summary.tldr: WorldCycle is a self-verifiable reinforcement learning framework that uses reversible action cycles to provide annotation-free supervision, reducing long-horizon video world model compounding errors without requiring ground-truth future states.
key_points: Uses closed action cycles and their inverse sequences to enforce that returning to an initial state requires zero analytical drift.
Optimizes a spatial closure reward to ensure symmetry between mirrored forward and reverse action segments.
Optimizes a temporal consistency reward to align states across repeated cycle executions, treating actions as consistent operators.
Introduces CycleBench, a diagnostic benchmark designed to test state-returning capabilities under complex action structures.
Reduces state-returning drift by up to 44% and increases composite-action accuracy nearly 4x over the base model.
summary.why_it_matters: It solves the verification bottleneck in post-training video world models, enabling more accurate, physically grounded long-horizon planning and exploration without manual annotations.

papers.title: SmartMage: Dynamic Modality Orchestration for 3D Scene Understanding

summary.tldr: SmartMage is a unified Multimodal Large Language Model that dynamically selects and routes heterogeneous visual and geometric modalities for 3D scene understanding based on query needs.
key_points: Semantic-guided Modality Adaptive RouTng (SMART) module selects task-relevant modalities using semantic priors, text-modality alignment, and modality quality.
Modality-Aware Gating Expert (MAGE) module uses modality priors to direct expert activation and enhance specialized multimodal reasoning.
Introduces ScanFacet, a diagnostic benchmark that categorizes tasks into fine-grained semantic types to analyze preferred modality combinations.
Achieves state-of-the-art results across five 3D scene understanding benchmarks and strong performance on RGB-only video benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the computational waste and semantic noise caused by fixed modality combinations, enabling more efficient and accurate 3D reasoning in embodied AI systems.

papers.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced the MIST benchmark, the SC2W susceptibility metric, and SCOPE, a DPO-based method that trains language models to selectively trust external context without blindly ignoring valid inputs.
key_points: MIST is a human-annotated benchmark presenting reasoning items across four matched conditions: clean, misleading, correct-context, and irrelevant-context.
SC2W is a paired metric measuring how frequently a misleading external signal converts a clean-correct response into an incorrect one.
SCOPE extracts clean-correct and misleading-wrong failure cases to optimize a Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) objective using preference pairs balanced across all four context conditions.
Universal susceptibility to misleading context was observed across models during the benchmark study.
SCOPE decreases SC2W while maintaining model accuracy on clean, correct, and irrelevant context inputs.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents language models from either blindly following deceptive context or becoming unhelpful by ignoring external context entirely.

papers.title: DASH: Divergence-Adaptive Supervision Horizons for On-Policy Self-Distillation of Reasoning Models

summary.tldr: DASH improves on-policy self-distillation for reasoning models by using adaptive propagation gates to dynamically weight token-level supervision based on how local teacher-student divergences evolve across time.
key_points: Identifies that standard On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) treats local divergences uniformly, ignoring the temporal sequence and discrepancy history of autoregressive rollouts.
Introduces Divergence-Adaptive Supervision Horizons (DASH), which maps the gap between local distillation signals and the sequence-level mean to adaptive propagation gates.
Uses these adaptive gates to control backward multi-step aggregation, dynamically adjusting supervision weights according to temporal divergence trends.

Reuses already-computed teacher and student distributions, achieving performance gains over vanilla OPSD across three mathematical reasoning benchmarks and three model scales with zero extra forward passes.
summary.why_it_matters: DASH increases the efficiency and accuracy of Dense RLVR self-distillation without introducing any additional computational overhead from extra forward passes.

papers.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision

summary.tldr: Unsupervised On-Policy Self-Distillation (U-OPSD) enables LLMs to self-correct without external supervision by distilling pseudo-solutions derived from self-consistency into prefixes of their longest incorrect completions.
key_points: Constructs pseudo-solutions from model generations using majority voting under a self-consistency threshold.
Conditions a teacher distribution on the shortest pseudo-solution and distills it into prefixes of the model's longest incorrect completion.
Improves Qwen3 non-thinking base models by 8.5% (4B) and 10.7% (8B) across math benchmarks, outperforming supervised OPSD by an average of 3.2% and 2.3%.
Matches or exceeds supervised methods in thinking mode, outperforming GRPO by 0.7% (4B) and 1.1% (8B) on AIME, HMMT25, MATH500, and AMC23 benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that LLM post-training and self-correction can match or exceed supervised baseline performance without relying on ground-truth labels, environmental feedback, or larger teacher models.

papers.title: MACRO: Markov Chain Routing of Transformer Layers

summary.tldr: MACRO enables parameter-free dynamic layer routing in LLMs by modeling layer execution paths as a context-dependent Markov policy decoded with a top-k Viterbi algorithm.
key_points: Learns task-specific execution routes across frozen LLM parameters without modifying underlying model weights or requiring test-time ground-truth labels.
Conditions its Markov policy on layer indices, budget phases, directional displacements, and operator contexts to execute skips, repeats, and residual additions.
Uses a top-k Viterbi decoding algorithm to efficiently identify high-probability candidate execution paths from training feedback.
Outperforms the dynamic routing baseline Dr. LLM by +7.2% in average accuracy while achieving a 9.4x reduction in route-search time (1.6 vs 14.8 hours).
Delivers a +5.0% average accuracy gain over unrouted baselines across open-weight LLMs, showing the largest improvements on smaller models.
summary.why_it_matters: MACRO provides a faster, parameter-free way to optimize dynamic inference paths in open-weight LLMs without retraining weights or adding heavy search latency.

papers.title: Hierarchical Latent Prediction for Language Models

summary.tldr: Hierarchical Latent Prediction (HiLP) introduces an auxiliary higher-level abstract latent to standard language model pre-training, mitigating compounding rollout errors in latent-space predictions.
key_points: Addresses limitations in Next-Token Prediction (NTP), Multi-Token Prediction (MTP), and Next-Latent prediction (NextLat), which suffer from short prediction horizons or compounding multi-step rollout errors.
Introduces an auxiliary higher-level abstract latent variable to stabilize multi-step rollouts and maintain long-horizon coherent belief state representations.
Demonstrates performance gains across coding and multi-step reasoning benchmarks.
Improves speculative decoding efficiency during inference.
summary.why_it_matters: HiLP enables language models to reason and plan over longer horizons while improving inference speed through more efficient speculative decoding.

papers.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games

summary.tldr: AV-AIVAT combines Action-Informed Value Assessment Tool variance reduction with continuously monitored Confidence Sequences to enable certified, anytime-valid early stopping in imperfect-information game evaluations.
key_points: AIVAT reduces variance in imperfect-information games by a median of 54x across 15 LLM agent configurations over 71,439 paired Heads-Up No-Limit Hold'em (HUNL) hands using conditional mean-zero corrections.
AV-AIVAT uses an online value model that trains solely on past games to prevent any game from scoring its own correction, preserving valid optional stopping.

At a nominal 95% confidence level and a target precision of +/-1 Big Blind, raw outcomes require a median 74x more hands to stop compared to AIVAT-corrected outcomes under the Asymptotic CS (AsympCS).
Exact finite-sample certification via the Empirical-Bernstein CS (EB-CS) relies on structurally established payoff bounds, showing a median 1.37x stopping-time ratio in descriptive HUNL runs.
summary.why_it_matters: It drastically cuts computation, model inference, and execution costs during agent evaluation by allowing evaluations to stop safely the exact moment statistical evidence is sufficient.

papers.title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping

summary.tldr: A new trace-grounded parametric profiling method reveals that Video Language Models fail at simple event counting, exhibiting a staged temporal failure driven by event representation, count, and frequency.
key_points: Evaluated models across 2,190 controlled videos with executable ground-truth traces across three tasks: bouncing-ball wall contacts, visual blinks, and state transitions.
At an 80% reliability threshold, Gemini 3.6 Flash counts persistent state transitions up to 12 events (at 0.5 and 1.0 Hz), but shows zero reliable positive-count regions for transient blinking.
In high-count, high-frequency scenarios, Gemini 3.6 Flash achieves only 0.2% count accuracy and recovers just 18.1% of true events.
Increasing the visual frame sampling rate improved Bounce Ball count accuracy from 19.6% to 29.3%, but true sequence agreement with ground truth remained at only 3.7%.
summary.why_it_matters: Aggregate accuracy metrics can mask severe temporal reasoning failures in video language models, as increased frame sampling may artificially inflate final scores without recovering actual event sequences.

papers.title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories

summary.tldr: TrajDebug is a framework that identifies critical failures in long-horizon LLM agent trajectories using multi-granularity history compression, evidence-based error detection, and error-lifecycle tracing to measure terminal impact.
key_points: Addresses long-horizon trajectory debugging challenges, including distant evidence scattering and differentiating benign local errors from critical failures.
Uses multi-granularity history compression and evidence-based identification to discover errors in long contexts.
Traces each error's resolution status and terminal impact to perform critical failure attribution.
Introduces TrajErrBench, containing 486 manually annotated failed trajectories from Tau2Bench and SWE-Bench Pro across tool-use and coding tasks.
Demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy over existing baselines and provides actionable feedback that improves downstream agent success rates.
summary.why_it_matters: TrajDebug allows developers to pinpoint the root cause of cascading failures in complex LLM agent trajectories, providing actionable diagnoses to increase downstream task completion rates.

papers.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced a reference-free framework that utilizes LLM judges to evaluate conversational-agent benchmarks based on consistency, complexity, and policy coverage.
key_points: Evaluates task-oriented conversational agent benchmarks across three dimensions: task consistency, scenario complexity, and policy coverage.
Uses a reference-free LLM-judge approach to provide actionable diagnostics on benchmark weaknesses.
Validated via agreement with human annotations, evaluation of LLM-generated benchmarks across model capabilities, and controlled quality-degrading perturbations.
Demonstrated effective quality-level discrimination on both synthetic and manually curated benchmarks across domains.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a standardized, automated way to diagnose and improve the quality of conversational agent benchmarks, ensuring more reliable performance evaluations.

papers.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization

summary.tldr: HarnessOpt-Bench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs on end-to-end, evaluation-guided harness optimization under strict budget and resource constraints.
key_points: Evaluates an optimizer LLM's ability to iteratively edit a target agent's prompts, tools, control flow, memory, and orchestration code given graded feedback.
Uses a trusted execution environment to enforce evaluation boundaries, meter resource usage, and evaluate final candidates on a held-out test partition.
Benchmarked 5 frontier LLMs across 4 downstream tasks over 111 scored runs, comparing both a shared coding harness and native harnesses.
Results indicate optimizer model capability creates larger performance variance than the choice of coding harness, with native harnesses showing inconsistent superiority.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized, discriminative framework to measure and improve an LLM's ability to automatically engineer and optimize agentic control systems.

security.title: Hardware Keystores for AI Agent Signing Workflows: A Zero-Trust MCP Enforcement Architecture

summary.tldr: A hardware keystore architecture uses PKCS#11 interfaces and a five-layer Zero-Trust stack to isolate private keys and prevent prompt injection-driven key usage in AI agents.
key_points: Replaces software-stored keys with hardware-confined keys (HSM, TPM, smart card) using opaque handles via vendor-neutral PKCS#11.
Enforces security via a five-layer stack: session identity (SAGA), scope bounds (Smax), semantic validation (RAV), taint tracking, and a hardware execution boundary.
Evaluated against 12 AgentDojo injection scenarios across four LLM models (gpt-oss-120b, Qwen2.5-72B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, and one other).
Reduced baseline Attack Success Rate (ASR) from 19.3% [14.3%, 25.4%] to 0% (95% CI upper bound 2.0%) with zero false positives on benign tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It completely blocks key exfiltration and unauthorized content signing by prompt injection attacks, fixing vulnerabilities where software keys can be stolen in under five minutes.

security.title: MMAligner: Safeguarding Multimodal Large Language Models through Representation Calibration

summary.tldr: MMAligner restores MLLM safety by calibrating unsafe multimodal representations back into the model's pre-existing text safety subspace and refusal boundary, achieving a 99% refusal rate on unsafe multimodal inputs with minimal utility loss.
key_points: Geometric analysis shows MLLMs retain a functional, shared text-multimodal safety subspace and refusal boundary, but unsafe multimodal inputs experience a representation shift outside this region.
MMAligner calibrates representations using a hard lower bound to enforce refusal, a soft upper bound to limit over-modification, and a preservation objective to protect benign inputs.
The method raises the average refusal rate on unsafe multimodal inputs to 99% across multiple open-source MLLMs while causing less than 2% utility degradation.
It eliminates the need for external guardrails or large-scale multimodal safety fine-tuning datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that MLLM safety failures stem from representation misalignment rather than lost safety capacity, offering an efficient, low-overhead method to patch multimodal jailbreaks without sacrificing model utility.

security.title: The Vulnerability With No CVE: Managing Persistent Gaps Between Mandate and Authority in AI Coding Agents

summary.tldr: This paper introduces the Agentic Posture Vulnerability (APV), a task-conditioned abstraction for managing durable security exposures caused by persistent gaps between an AI coding agent's mandate and authority.
key_points: Defines the Agentic Posture Vulnerability (APV) as a durable record linking varying task-level runtime manifestations to an invariant, underlying control exposure.
Operationalizes existing weaknesses, including excessive agency, improper authorization, and flawed control composition, without acting as a new root-cause risk class.
Differentiates APVs from CVE-addressable software defects, OWASP Excessive Agency definitions, and transient authorization-execution gaps.
Outlines structural implementation details including six recurring APV patterns, a thresholded definition, a minimal record schema, a vulnerability lifecycle, and a control-and-closure matrix.
summary.why_it_matters: It gives security teams a structured framework to track, manage, and remediate persistent configuration exposures in AI agents that traditional CVE tracking fails to address.

authors: Shayell Aharon Salomon Amir Shaked Matan Noga

security.title: Algebraic Cryptanalytic Extraction on Hard-Label Neural Networks

summary.tldr: A new algebraic model extraction framework uses an Approximate Signature Vector method to drastically speed up hard-label attacks on FCNNs and enable the first extraction of max-pooling CNNs.
key_points: Replaces SVD-based rank checking from Carlini et al.'s EUROCRYPT 2025 attack with simple inner-product operations using an Approximate Signature Vector (ASV) method.
Reduces the dual-point clustering time complexity from O(n^2 * (d^(k))^3) to an average of O(n * (d^(k))^3).
Leverages the properties that high-dimensional random vectors are nearly orthogonal and practical DNN neurons learn disentangled features.
Introduces a kernel-centric clustering scheme to execute the first hard-label model extraction attack against max-pooling CNNs (e.g., LeNet-5) by exploiting weight sharing.
Validated empirically on a 64-64x4-10 FCNN and LeNet-5 CNN architecture.
summary.why_it_matters: By removing the severe SVD computational bottleneck and expanding attack capabilities to CNNs, this work makes practical, real-world model extraction against hard-label black-box neural networks significantly more feasible.

security.title: DreamGuard: Efficient Runtime Guardrail for LLM Agents via Risk-Aware World Model

summary.tldr: DreamGuard is a proactive runtime guardrail for LLM agents that uses a risk-aware world model with a compact recurrent latent state to evaluate long-horizon hazards and intervene before action execution.
key_points: Maintains a compact recurrent latent state over the agent trajectory to predict future latent states.
Fuses multi-horizon signals—specifically immediate-hazard and prefix-risk evidence—to make pre-execution intervention decisions.
Achieves an average end-to-end latency of 25 ms per call while providing an improved safety-utility trade-off compared to reactive and proactive baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents cumulative, long-horizon risk drift from benign-looking actions in autonomous LLM agents with negligible latency overhead.

security.title: Breaking Customized LLMs for Coding: Automated Red Teaming for Instruction Backdoor Attacks

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced ARIA, an automated red-teaming framework that uses an attacker LLM to generate covert instruction backdoor attacks against customized LLMs for code intelligence tasks without modifying underlying model parameters.
key_points: ARIA uses an iterative attacker LLM guided by target model feedback on stealthiness, clean-task utility, and backdoor effectiveness.
Evaluations across four LLMs and three code intelligence tasks demonstrated a maximum attack success rate of 0.945 while preserving clean-task performance.
The attack achieves up to a 1.000 false negative rate against platform-side and user-side detection mechanisms and bypasses existing defenses.
ARIA generalizes across different programming languages and maintains robustness against variations in generation temperature.
summary.why_it_matters: It reveals that prompt-customized LLMs can be silently compromised using automated, highly covert backdoor instructions that easily evade current inspection methods and defenses.

security.title: Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced AMS, an Activation-based Model Scanner that detects safety training modifications in language models by analyzing activation-space geometry, achieving 71% cross-validation accuracy across 14 model configurations.
key_points: AMS categorizes safety modifications into a four-class taxonomy: training removal, weight-orthogonalization abliteration, rotation-without-collapse abliteration, and behavioral fine-tuning.
Detection relies on a two-tier system: Tier 1 sigma-thresholding detects cluster collapse, while Tier 2 direction-similarity verification detects refusal direction rotations.
Validation across Llama, Gemma, Qwen, and Mistral families shows the harmful-content concept sigma correlates with behavioral compliance at Pearson r = -0.546 (p = 0.043).
Behavioral fine-tuning preserves activation magnitude and direction, representing an activation-only undetectable failure mode.
summary.why_it_matters: AMS provides a mechanistic, activation-based auditing tool to verify whether open-weight language models have undergone safety striping or abliteration without relying solely on behavioral prompting.

security.title: When Experience Becomes Instruction: Trajectory Poisoning in Self-Evolving Agent Skill Systems

summary.tldr: PoisonedEvolution demonstrates trajectory-poisoning attacks on self-evolving skill (SES) systems, exploiting the evidence promotion process to embed targeted behaviors into persistent skill banks.
key_points: Artifact poisoning requires three conditions: Inclusion, Evolution Attribution (the main bottleneck requiring causal usefulness, recurrence, and generalizability), and Realization.
At 10% attacker support, PoisonedEvolution achieved a 91.0% Success Evocation Rate (SER) across six LLM evolvers in SkillClaw (546/600 trials).
The attack transferred to the structurally different Trace2Skill pipeline, achieving a 61.5% SER (369/600 trials) at the same 10% attacker ratio.

Controlled studies showed three consistent attacker records in a 30-record batch are sufficient for success, with key determinants being recurring support, causal framing, and domain-aligned encoding.
summary.why_it_matters: This vulnerability establishes evidence promotion as a critical security boundary, showing that malicious untrusted trajectory data can easily become trusted persistent instructions in autonomous LLM systems.

security.title: PromptShield Home: Ambient Multimodal Prompt Injection Defense for Smart-Home Agents

summary.tldr: PromptShield-Home is a benchmark evaluating smart-home MLLMs against ambient prompt injections across three abstraction layers: traditional detectors (L0), single MLLMs (L1), and multi-agent mediation (L2).
key_points: Evaluated layers show opposing failure modes: L0 traditional detectors execute blindly, while L1/L2 MLLM configurations suffer from severe over-refusal and missed critical events like fall detection.
Standard aggregate accuracy is misleading due to class imbalance, where a naive always-block baseline achieves 82% accuracy.
An oracle combining the disjoint correct prediction sets of L0 and L1/L2 reaches 94.1% accuracy, compared to 76.5% for the best individual layer.
Results demonstrate that MLLMs alone are currently inadequate for smart-home security, favoring learned routing and sensor fusion over full MLLM replacement.
summary.why_it_matters: Smart-home safety requires combining traditional detectors with MLLMs via learned routing, as relying solely on MLLMs leads to severe over-refusal and missed safety-critical events.

security.title: Adversarial Clothing Designed to Fool Facial Recognition Systems

summary.tldr: Commercial adversarial clothing featuring complex patterns claims to evade facial recognition algorithms, but experts warn these products lack rigorous testing and reliability.
key_points: Adversarial clothing uses targeted visual patterns to disrupt and confuse facial recognition detection algorithms.
Experts emphasize that current commercial options are untested, unverified, and largely function as security theater or symbolic fashion statements.
The anti-surveillance properties of these pattern-based designs are inherently fragile and can be rendered obsolete by minor updates to facial recognition software.
summary.why_it_matters: Relying on unverified adversarial fashion gives users a false sense of privacy against real-world, constantly updating surveillance systems.

security.title: Robust Context-Aware Detection of Malicious Instructions in Text

summary.tldr: CAD is a context- and query-aware detector for malicious sentences in text, combined with two adversarial training methods to defend LLM agents against indirect prompt injection and adaptive evasion attacks.
key_points: Introduces segment-level, context- and query-aware sentence classification to identify Indirect Prompt Injections (IPI).
Employs feature-space adversarial training (AT) using projected-gradient-based optimization in the embedding space to approximate evasions.
Simulates realizable adaptive evasion attacks within the AT loop using LLM-based paraphrasing.
Parametrizes both AT variants to enable a tunable tradeoff between general utility and attack robustness, with optimal parameters varying by application domain.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a robust, domain-tunable defense against indirect prompt injections and adaptive evasion attacks targeting LLM-based autonomous agents.

infra.title: Configure rate limits for AI traffic on AgentCore gateway

summary.tldr: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway now supports per-user rate limiting using request, connection, and token-based metrics across its target types.
key_points: Supports three rate limit metrics: Requests per second/minute (RPS/RPM) for all targets, Tokens per minute (TPM) for inference targets, and Connections per second (CPS) for tracking concurrent long-lived sessions.
TPM limits deduct upfront token estimates using a general-purpose tokenizer, reconciling with true input/output token counts reported by the model provider upon response.
Enables granular per-user control across MCP, inference, and HTTP passthrough targets using OAuth or IAM-based rules combined with AgentCore Identity JWTs and RBAC policies.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents AI tool and model exhaustion by controlling traffic throughput, token costs, and long-lived streaming connections per user group.

summary.tldr: Anthropic updated Claude Fable 5's biology safeguards to improve classifier accuracy, reducing false positives and biology-related model fallbacks by approximately 85%.
key_points: Classifier updates reduced biology-related fallbacks—where queries trigger a switch to a less capable model—by ~85% in testing.
The updates allow Fable 5 to handle more routine health, educational, and clinical tasks, such as interpreting lab results and understanding symptoms.
Fable 5 still falls back to Opus 5 for high-risk dual-use biological requests, including virology, toxicology, and molecular design.
Anthropic is developing trusted access pathways to eventually enable professional biology research and drug development while mitigating dual-use risks like biological weapon development.
summary.why_it_matters: Users and healthcare professionals experience significantly fewer model downgrades on safe biological and clinical queries while high-risk dual-use topics remain restricted.
